rubrics.title: Pilot writing goals
rubrics.purpose: Explain a conclusion and its reasons clearly.

criteria.name: Conciseness
criteria.question: Does repeated explanation add a distinct point?

levels.label: Little alignment
levels.description: The passage repeats explanation without adding a distinct reason, example, or qualification.

levels.label: Some alignment
levels.description: The passage mixes distinct additions with repeated explanation.

levels.label: Strong alignment
levels.description: The passage develops its point without repetition that adds no distinct point.

criteria.name: Explicit support
criteria.question: Are important conclusions supported by reasons in the supplied text?

levels.label: Little alignment
levels.description: Important conclusions have no supporting reason in the supplied text.

levels.label: Some alignment
levels.description: Some conclusions have supporting reasons, but important gaps remain.

levels.label: Strong alignment
levels.description: Important conclusions have explicit, relevant supporting reasons.

criteria.name: Audience accessibility
criteria.question: Can the named audience understand essential terms in the target, using the supplied context?

levels.label: Little alignment
levels.description: Essential terms are unexplained for the named audience.

levels.label: Some alignment
levels.description: Some essential terms are explained, while others remain unclear for the named audience.

levels.label: Strong alignment
levels.description: Essential terms are understandable for the named audience using the supplied text.

criteria.name: Document consistency
criteria.question: Does the complete draft make internally consistent claims?

levels.label: Little alignment
levels.description: The draft makes directly conflicting claims without resolving the conflict.

levels.label: Some alignment
levels.description: Claims appear in tension, with partial qualification.

levels.label: Strong alignment
levels.description: The draft makes compatible claims or explicitly resolves apparent conflicts.
